declared_use_included_in_minimum_fee.text: Upon payment of the minimum fees the producer gets worldwide non-theatrical use plus ONE declared use: theatrical (worldwide, for the period of copyright); free TV (one domestic run in Canada); pay TV (one year in Canada); cable TV (three years in Canada); compact devices (two years in Canada); educational TV (three years in Canada); new media (worldwide one year for Option 1 New Media productions at $11,735/minute or less, or over that where a prepayment or advance is elected); High-Budget SVOD and other Option 1 New Media productions get a six-month worldwide declared use.

residual_payments_percent_of_net_fees.rule: If the production is used outside its declared use and the producer has NOT elected the B5 prepayment/advance system, performers are paid these percentages of their Net Fees, within 30 days of the use.

free_tv_canada.note: Once single-station payments reach 30% of Net Fees, one broadcast on one station in each unused Canadian market is allowed.

free_tv_world_market.note: Read from layout-extracted text; percentages appear in a single column in order 10%, 5%, 4%, 2%.

pay_tv.note: Mapped from the column order 10%, 25%, 15%, 30%, 5%, 30% in the extracted PDF text. The foreign 12-month figure of 30% against 5% for three months looks irregular; verify against the printed page before relying on the foreign pair.

new_media_per_year.note: This is the 'Internet'/streaming use under the fixed-percentage system (B408).

all_uses_prepayment_B501a.covers: all media worldwide including New Media
all_uses_prepayment_B501a.term: 4 consecutive years from first exploitation in any residual market

conventional_use_prepayment_B501b.covers: all media worldwide excluding New Media
conventional_use_prepayment_B501b.term: 4 consecutive years from first exploitation in any conventional residual market

prepayment_and_advance_options.rule: Prepayment must be declared in each performer's contract and paid at the time of production; the same option and percentage must apply to every performer on the production (B503).

options.limit: Only if all presales as of day one of principal photography are exclusively Canadian and include a declared use (B502).

advance_option_B501c.mechanics: Non-refundable advance paid at production; no DGR payments until the aggregate advance is recouped from DGR (B505). An individual's advance credited is capped at 50% of that performer's Gross Fees (B506); a performer's credited advance is also capped at days of principal photography x 12 x the B101 Principal Actor daily minimum (B507). Not available to purely foreign service series.

animation_extra_options_D111.perpetuity_excluding_theatrical_and_new_: 200% of Net Fees; a later theatrical use pays 3.6% of DGR from first dollar
animation_extra_options_D111.perpetuity_excluding_theatrical_includin: 205% of Net Fees; a later theatrical use pays 3.6% of DGR from first dollar

documentary_B601.conventional_5_year: at least 50% of Net Fees, renewable for another 5 years at 50% or switch to 3.6% of DGR
documentary_B601.all_uses_5_year: at least 55% of Net Fees, renewable at 55% or switch to 3.6% of DGR

dgr_formula.after_prepayment_B504a: 3.6% of DGR in aggregate to all performers after the 4-year prepaid window (revenue earned inside the prepaid window is excluded from DGR). 5% for CIPIP productions; 8% for Option 1 New Media productions budgeted at $111,735 per minute or less (as printed in B504(a)).
dgr_formula.new_media_after_conventional_prepayment_: If a conventional (no New Media) prepayment was elected and the production is later exploited in New Media, performers get 3.6% of DGR (5% for CIPIP) from the date of first New Media exploitation.
dgr_formula.high_budget_svod_E204: Netflix-type High-Budget SVOD productions (thresholds: $1,475,000+ for 20-35 min, $2,825,000+ for 36-65 min, $3,400,000+ for 66+ min): New Media prepayment of 105% of Net Fees buys 4 years beyond the declared-use period, then 3.6% of DGR; or All Uses prepayment (B501a) then 3.6%; or an advance. With no election, 3.6% of DGR from New Media revenue after the 6-month declared use.
dgr_formula.new_media_tiers_C_D_E108: 8% of DGR after the declared use or after a 105% four-year New Media prepayment.
dgr_formula.dgr_definition_B509: All monies from distribution of the production, from first dollar, with no deduction of expenses; excludes merchandising, novelization and sequel rights; presales included; distributor advances not included for triggering; for animation only English-language licence revenue counts; EST and physical disc DGR deemed 20% of wholesale price (10% if wholesale is at or below about $30/unit).

flows_through_actra_prs.detail: Additional use fees are payable to the ACTRA PRS and distributed to performers under B512 (B508). B512: one unit = the minimum fee for the lowest-rated residual category for one day; each performer gets units by Gross Fee earned on the production, capped at 20 units; the production's total revenue is divided by total units to set a dollar value per unit.
flows_through_actra_prs.prs_admin_fees: Producer remits 0.5% of Gross Fees to ACTRA PRS (max $250 per episode / $1,500 per season for a series; $1,500 for other productions) (A3702a), plus 1% of amounts PRS distributes, minimum $150 per production (A3702b).
flows_through_actra_prs.bc_exception: In British Columbia, residuals for UBCP/ACTRA productions are administered by UBCP/ACTRA rather than ACTRA PRS (ubcp_residuals page).

non_member_equalization.value: Producer contributes 12% of Gross Fees (2025-01-26 to 2025-12-31) and 12.5% (2026-01-01 to 2026-12-31) for each non-member, apprentice or work permittee, to a maximum of $3,000 per performer per production (or per series cycle).
non_member_equalization.note: This is paid to ACTRA by the producer, not to the performer.

share_of_performers_receiving_residuals.note: No published rule of thumb for the share of performers who receive residuals was found on ACTRA, ACTRA Toronto, UBCP/ACTRA, ACTRA PRS, AQPM or CMPA pages. The PRS landing page and the IPA 101 article give no such statistic. The only aggregate found: 'Last year ACTRA PRS distributed more than $20 million to performers.'

aggregate_figure.value: more than $20 million distributed by ACTRA PRS in a year

share_of_performers_receiving_residuals.structural_note: Structurally, B512's per-performer cap of 20 units and pro-rata distribution mean every contracted performer on a production that earns post-window DGR shares in it; whether a given production ever pays out depends on whether it earns DGR beyond the prepaid window or recoups the advance. No figure is invented here.

non_member_work_permit.ipa_agreement_text_A701: Principal performers who are Canadian citizens or permanent residents pay $260.00 for the first week and $260.00 for each later week; other performers (not background) $210.00 per week; the producer is not required to pay; ACTRA may amend the fee on 90 days' notice. A non-Canadian non-member pays $260.00 for the first week and $175.00 for each later week. A week is seven consecutive days from the first contracted day.
non_member_work_permit.ipa_answer: Under the IPA the permit is charged per week of engagement, not per engagement: $260.00 per week for a principal, $210.00 per week for an actor. It is paid by the performer, and the same fee applies to apprentices and non-members (the ACTRA Toronto IPA table makes no apprentice/non-member distinction).
